review_candidates.title: Associate, Research & Market Intelligence
review_candidates.description: A transaction often begins long before anyone calls it a transaction. It begins when someone notices that a founder may be ready to sell. That a sector is consolidating. That a company has quietly changed ownership. That a multinational is entering a new market. That a private equity fund is approaching the end of its holding period. That a business is raising capital. That a government is changing regulation. That a company nobody is talking about has become one of the most interesting assets in its sector. Seeing those things early matters. Understanding what they mean matters even more. 0to1 Advisory is looking for an exceptional Associate, Research & Market Intelligence to help us build the intelligence behind our transaction, investment and advisory work across Africa. This is not a desk research job. It is an apprenticeship in understanding markets, companies, capital and opportunity. Why this role is unusual 0to1 is building a small, senior led advisory firm working across transactions, investments, capital markets, value creation and sovereign and development finance. As an Associate, you will work directly with the founding team rather than several layers removed from decision making. The team brings experience across strategy, advisory, enterprise transformation, development finance, public sector work and international institutions including the World Bank and USAID. You will also work alongside and learn from an independent bench of senior advisers that includes former executives and leaders from major listed companies in Africa and the United States. That means the research you produce will not disappear into a folder. It will be challenged by people who have run companies, invested capital, advised institutions and made the kinds of decisions you are researching. That is part of the apprenticeship. What you will actually do One week you might be asked: Which manufacturing companies in East Africa could fit a US investor's acquisition mandate? The next: Which institutional investors are most likely to invest in a growing African financial services company? Then: Who are the serious competitors in this market and who actually controls distribution? Or: Which African companies could credibly prepare for a public markets transaction over the next three years? Those questions sound simple. They rarely are. You will need to understand ownership, management, financial scale, capital history, sector dynamics, regulation, competitors, strategic fit, investor behaviour and sometimes information that is not neatly available online. You will: • map companies, sectors and investment landscapes • build acquisition and investment target lists • screen companies against client mandates • research ownership and shareholder structures • analyse investors, private equity funds, family offices, DFIs and strategic buyers • track capital raises, acquisitions, exits, IPOs, management changes and ownership transitions • conduct competitor and market structure analysis • analyse market entry opportunities • map regional supply chains • research regulation and country considerations • support commercial and strategic diligence • develop company and sector profiles • identify transaction signals before they become obvious • speak with industry participants and market sources where public information is insufficient • turn large amounts of information into short, useful conclusions for clients and transaction teams The objective is to know what matters . Why Africa makes this role different Many of the world's most established markets are already deeply mapped. Africa is different. Information is fragmented. Ownership is often opaque. Companies can be much larger or more sophisticated than their public footprint suggests. Important businesses may have very little online presence. Relationships matter. Context matters. Local knowledge matters. That makes serious market intelligence extraordinarily valuable. It also makes Africa one of the most interesting places in the world to build this skill. You will gain first hand exposure to businesses and investment opportunities across African markets at the point when global capital, demographic growth, industrialisation, digital transformation and new capital market structures are beginning to intersect. For someone who wants a career in private equity, investment banking, corporate development, investment research or strategic finance, this is an unusual place to learn. The frontier questions We are particularly interested in people who are curious about questions that are not yet fully answered. Where will the next generation of African mid market companies come from? Which sectors are moving from family ownership to institutional ownership? Where will private equity exits come from? Which African companies could become regional champions? How will AI affect productivity and enterprise value? How will new exchanges and cross border capital markets change African financing? Where will global supply chain shifts create new African winners? Which companies today could become tomorrow's acquisition targets, IPO candidates or institutional portfolio businesses? This role sits close to those questions. Who should apply You may come from: investment research private equity investment banking consulting transaction advisory corporate strategy economic research equity research competitive intelligence corporate finance data or business analysis You may also be a CFA candidate, CPA, economist or finance professional trying to move closer to the investment and transaction world. What matters most is how your mind works. You should be the sort of person who: notices things other people overlook asks one more question checks the original source does not confuse information with understanding gets suspicious when everybody is repeating the same fact can look at fifty companies and explain why three matter and enjoys figuring out how businesses actually make money. How we work This is a hybrid role based in Nairobi . We do not believe good thinking is produced by attendance sheets. There will be moments when being together matters enormously, particularly around clients, live transactions and intensive team work. There will also be periods where deep research is better done without unnecessary ceremony. We measure people primarily by the quality, reliability and usefulness of their work. With that freedom comes a high expectation of ownership. What you can expect from us You will receive: direct access to the founding team mentorship from senior advisers and experienced business leaders exposure to live transactions and investment decisions Africa wide company and sector exposure contact with investors, executives, advisers and institutions the opportunity to develop genuine investment judgement significant responsibility earlier than you would typically receive in a large institution the opportunity to help build 0to1's proprietary intelligence base exposure to new areas at the intersection of capital, companies, markets and technology This role will suit someone who does not simply want a job in research. It will suit someone who wants to learn how opportunities are found before everyone else sees them. Location: Nairobi based, hybrid Level: Associate Firm: 0to1 Advisory How to apply Send us your CV and answer one question in no more than one page: Choose one African company, sector or market that you believe serious investors should be paying more attention to over the next five years. What are others missing? We care less about whether we agree with you than whether you can make us think.
